paper.title: Prior-Free Competitive Ratios for Improving Bandits: Scale, Curvature and Horizon Are Free, but Not Jointly Under Noise

settings.name_in_paper: Improving multi-armed bandits (noiseless), known horizon, scale-oblivious
unmapped: Rested improving arms: t-th pull of arm i yields f_i(t), f_i nonnegative, nondecreasing, discretely concave with f_i(0)=0
Objective is competitive ratio OPT_T/E[ALG_T] against best single arm
Learner does not know scale m=f*(T) nor envelope exponent beta
settings.definition_quote: An instance consists of $k$ arms; arm $i$ has a reward function $f_i:\{0,1,\dots,T\}\to\R_{\ge0}$ with $f_i(0)=0$, nondecreasing, and with \emph{diminishing returns}... The adversary is \emph{oblivious}.

settings.name_in_paper: Improving multi-armed bandits (noiseless), unknown horizon (anytime), scale-oblivious
unmapped: Rested improving arms with nondecreasing discretely concave reward curves
Objective is competitive ratio against best single arm
Learner does not know scale m nor envelope exponent beta
settings.definition_quote: An algorithm is ... \emph{anytime} if it does not read $T$.

settings.name_in_paper: Improving bandits (noiseless), known envelope exponent beta, unknown scale, known horizon
unmapped: Rested improving arms with concave nondecreasing curves; competitive ratio objective
Comparator arm satisfies lower envelope LE(beta): f(t) >= f(T)(t/T)^beta
Learner knows envelope exponent beta
settings.definition_quote: for $\beta\in(0,1]$ we say that arm $i$ satisfies $\LE(\beta)$ if the inequality $f_i(t)\ge f_i(T)\,(t/T)^\beta$ holds for all $t\le T$.

settings.name_in_paper: Improving bandits (noiseless), known beta, unknown horizon
unmapped: Rested improving arms with concave nondecreasing curves; competitive ratio objective
Comparator satisfies LE(beta); learner knows beta
settings.definition_quote: with $T$ unknown: for $k\ge2$ and $s=\lceil K_\beta\rceil$, independent $\PC$ phases...

settings.name_in_paper: Improving bandits with multiplicative noise, known horizon, scale- and noise-oblivious
unmapped: Rested improving arms with concave nondecreasing curves; competitive ratio objective
Multiplicative adversarial noise: observed/earned reward in [(1-eps)f_i(t),(1+eps)f_i(t)], fixed obliviously, eps unknown to learner
Learner knows neither scale m nor beta nor eps
settings.definition_quote: we get a reward value $\hat f_i(t_i)\in[(1-\varepsilon)f_i(t_i),(1+\varepsilon)f_i(t_i)]$; the algorithm observes and earns $\hat f$. The noisy values are fixed by the oblivious adversary before the run

settings.name_in_paper: Improving bandits with multiplicative noise, unknown horizon
unmapped: Rested improving arms; competitive ratio objective
Multiplicative oblivious noise of unknown level eps
Learner knows neither m, beta, eps nor T
settings.definition_quote: Let $A$ be the algorithm that, before the run, selects uniformly at random one of the three anytime algorithms... It reads none of $m,\beta,T,\varepsilon$

settings.name_in_paper: Improving bandits with multiplicative noise, scale and beta unknown (lower bound)
unmapped: Rested improving arms; competitive ratio against noisy benchmark hat R
Multiplicative oblivious noise with fixed eps in (0,1/2]; learner may know eps
Learner does not know scale m nor envelope exponent beta
settings.definition_quote: every algorithm that does not read $m$ or $\beta$ (it may read $T$ and $\varepsilon$)

settings.name_in_paper: Improving bandits with multiplicative noise, known scale m
unmapped: Rested improving arms; competitive ratio
Multiplicative oblivious noise with eps <= 1/2 unknown
Learner is given the scale m=f*(T) of the comparator arm, not beta
settings.definition_quote: $\RET(H,\mu)$ (random-exponent elimination); reads $k$, $H$ and a scale $\mu$; not $\beta$ or $\varepsilon$.

settings.name_in_paper: Improving bandits with multiplicative noise, known upper bound on noise level
unmapped: Rested improving arms; competitive ratio
Multiplicative oblivious noise; learner knows an upper bound eps_bar >= eps
Learner knows neither m nor beta
settings.definition_quote: which reads $k$, $T$ and any valid upper bound $\bar\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon$ on the noise level --- but neither $m$, nor $\beta$, nor $\varepsilon$ itself

algorithms.name: Uniform mixture of APC, phased NPA and anytime SRMP

source.label: thm:TA
source.quote: Let $k\ge2$, $T\ge2\lfloor\sqrt k\rfloor$, $s=\lfloor\sqrt k\rfloor$, $\tau=\lfloor T/(2s)\rfloor$. Then $\PC(s,\tau)$ satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{s}{8k}R\ge\frac{R}{16\sqrt k}$, and in fact $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{R}{4\sqrt3\,\sqrt k}$.

results.notes: Competitive ratio OPT/E[ALG]; bound stated as E[ALG] >= R/(4 sqrt3 sqrt k), recorded as ratio upper bound.

tuning: s = min(floor(sqrt K), floor(T/2)), tau = floor(T/(2s)); uniform random arm if T=1

source.label: thm:allT
source.quote: For all integers $k,T\ge1$, the minimax ratio of scale-oblivious algorithms satisfies $\frac14\Big(\sqrt k+\frac kT\Big)\le\rho(k,T)\le24\Big(\sqrt k+\frac kT\Big)$.

results.notes: Upper bound via PC with truncated parameters.

source.label: thm:allT
source.quote: For all integers $k,T\ge1$, the minimax ratio of scale-oblivious algorithms satisfies $\frac14\Big(\sqrt k+\frac kT\Big)\le\rho(k,T)\le24\Big(\sqrt k+\frac kT\Big)$.

results.notes: Holds for all randomized algorithms (from Corollary 3.7), even if scale known.

conditions: instances with linear good arm and truncated decoys

source.label: cor:L4
source.quote: For every randomized algorithm there is an instance on which its competitive ratio is at least (a) $\sqrt k/3$, for all $k,T\ge1$ (take $g(t)=t/T$, $d=\lfloor T/\sqrt k\rfloor$); and (b) $k/T$

results.notes: Restatement with integer bookkeeping of BR25 argument; part (a).

conditions: one linear arm and K-1 zero arms

source.label: cor:L4
source.quote: (b) $k/T$ (take $g(t)=t/T$, $d=0$: one linear arm and $k-1$ arms identically zero).

results.notes: Part (b).

source.label: thm:anytime
source.quote: Let $s=\lfloor\sqrt k\rfloor$ and run phases of lengths $L_j=2s\cdot2^j$... The algorithm reads only $k$, and for every $T\ge2s$, $\E[\ALG_T]\ge R/(256\sqrt k)$.

source.label: thm:anytimeAll
source.quote: For all integers $k,T\ge1$, $\APC$ satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{R}{1536\,(\sqrt k+k/T)}$.

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1] of LE(beta)

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: Let $\beta\in(0,1]$ be known and suppose the comparator arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$. For $k\ge2$, $T\ge2\lceil K_\beta\rceil$, $s=\lceil K_\beta\rceil$, $\tau=\lfloor T/(2s)\rfloor$, $\PC(s,\tau)$ satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge R/(16k^{\gamma})$.

results.notes: gamma = beta/(1+beta).

conditions: all arms satisfy LE(beta_env), envelope exponent exactly beta_env

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: for every $k\ge2$ and $T\ge2$ there is an explicit distribution over instances, all of whose arms satisfy $\LE(\beta)$ ... hence for every algorithm some instance of that family forces ratio at least $k^\gamma/(\beta+2)$

results.notes: Holds for every algorithm, even knowing beta and m.

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: for all $T\ge1$, $\frac{k^\gamma+k/T}{\beta+3}\le\rho_\beta(k,T)\le24(k^\gamma+k/T)$

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: for all $T\ge1$, $\frac{k^\gamma+k/T}{\beta+3}\le\rho_\beta(k,T)\le24(k^\gamma+k/T)$

source.label: thm:TD
source.quote: with $T$ unknown: for $k\ge2$ and $s=\lceil K_\beta\rceil$, independent $\PC$ phases of lengths $2s\cdot2^j$ ... give $\E[\ALG_T]\ge R/(128k^\gamma)$ for every $T\ge2s$

results.notes: Algorithm is doubling PC with beta-tuned s.

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1] satisfied by optimal arm (unknown to algorithm)

source.label: thm:TG
source.quote: Let $k\ge2$, $\beta\in(0,1]$, $T\ge16k$, and suppose the optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$. Then $\RMP(T)$, which reads neither $m$ nor $\beta$, satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{3}{256}\,R\,k^{-\beta/(1+\beta)}$.

results.notes: Holds simultaneously for all beta. Also gives a depth-oracle guarantee (3/1024)min{f*(d)/m, T/(kd)}, not separately recorded.

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1] of optimal arm

source.label: thm:TGp
source.quote: Run $\RMP(H_j)$ in phases $H_j=16k\cdot2^j$ ... The algorithm reads only $k$, and for every $\beta\in(0,1]$, every instance whose optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, and every $T\ge16k$, $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{3}{4096}Rq_\beta$.

results.notes: Corollary 4.7 restates price of priors constants (128, 2048) and is not recorded separately.

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1] of optimal arm

source.label: thm:W46
source.quote: For all integers $k,T\ge1$, all $\beta\in(0,1]$ and all instances whose optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, $\SRMP(k,T)$ satisfies $\E[\ALG_T]\ge\frac{R}{c_{\mathrm{SR}}}\min\Big\{k^{-\beta/(1+\beta)},\ \frac Tk\Big\}$, $c_{\mathrm{SR}}:=2^{13}=8192$.

results.notes: Theorem also states ratio <= c_SR(k^gamma + k/T) and matching lower bound from Thm 3.13(ii).

symbols.beta_env: envelope exponent beta in (0,1] of optimal arm

source.label: thm:W47
source.quote: Run $\SRMP$ in phases of lengths $1,2,4,\dots$, each with fresh randomness... The algorithm reads only $k$, and for every $T\ge1$, $\E[\ALG_T]\ge2^{-19}\,R\,Q_\beta(k,T)$.

results.notes: Q_beta = min{K^-gamma, T/K}.

source.label: thm:H1
source.quote: Let $\PC$ commit to the arm with the largest observed probe value. For every instance and admissible $(s,\tau)$, $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{b}\,R\,\min\{\frac{r\tau}{T^2},\frac{s\,r(r+1)}{2kT^2}\}$. ... each algorithm of Section~3 keeps its guarantee up to the factor $a^2/b$

results.notes: Table row PC, T known: CG=16 sqrt k. Against hat R the ratio has extra factor b. Other table rows (doubling PC 256 sqrt k, beta-known rows) not separately recorded.

source.label: thm:H1
source.quote: $\PC$, truncated parameters (Thm.~3.8) & $24(\sqrt k+k/T)$ & all $T\ge1$ ... the noisy minimax ratio of scale-oblivious algorithms is $\Theta(\sqrt k+k/T)$ at every horizon

results.notes: Table row of Theorem 5.1.

source.label: thm:H1
source.quote: $\APC$, $T$ unknown (Thm.~3.12) & $1536(\sqrt k+k/T)$ & all $T\ge1$

results.notes: Table row of Theorem 5.1.

source.label: thm:H2U
source.quote: For every $\beta\in(0,1]$, every instance whose optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, and $T\ge16k$, $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{64b}\,\frac{R\,q_\beta}{\PhiK(k)}\ge\frac{a^2}{64b^2}\,\frac{\hat R\,q_\beta}{\PhiK(k)}$. With $T$ unknown ... the constant becomes $1024$.

results.notes: Anytime phased version has constant 1024 instead of 64.

source.label: thm:H2U
source.quote: With $T$ unknown (phases $16k\cdot2^j$, conditioning on history as in Lemma~4.5) the constant becomes $1024$.

results.notes: Interpreted as 64 replaced by 1024.

source.label: thm:H2L
source.quote: For every $k\ge k_0(\varepsilon)$ and every algorithm that does not read $m$ or $\beta$ (it may read $T$ and $\varepsilon$), there exist $\beta\in(0,1]$, an instance whose optimal arm satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, and a fixed in-band noise table such that $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\le\frac{8192}{\varepsilon\,\PhiK(k)}\,\hat R\,q_\beta$.

results.notes: Algorithm class: algorithms not reading m or beta. Ratio hat R/E >= eps Phi(K) K^gamma/8192 for adversarially chosen beta.

source.label: thm:RET
source.quote: In particular, when the scale of a cumulatively optimal arm is known --- take $H=T$ and $\mu=m=f_\ast(T)$ ... we get $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac a{2048b}Rq_\beta$ simultaneously for every such $\beta$, without reading $\beta$ or $\varepsilon$

results.notes: Unknown-T phased version gives 32768 in the advice model.

conditions: scale advice tied to evaluation horizon

source.label: thm:RET
source.quote: If in addition $T$ is unknown, running $\RET(H_j,\mu)$ in phases $H_j=16k\cdot2^j$ with the advice $\mu=m/4$ gives $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac a{32768\,b}Rq_\beta$ for every $T\ge16k$

results.notes: Learner does not read T but receives scale advice m for the evaluation horizon; setting s8 lists T known, slight mismatch.

symbols.c_eps: (1+eps_bar)/(1-eps_bar) - (1-eps_bar)/(1+eps_bar) for supplied noise upper bound eps_bar

source.label: prop:W48
source.quote: There is an algorithm $\SRMPc$ ... which reads $k$, $T$ and any valid upper bound $\bar\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon$ ... and which satisfies, for all integers $k,T\ge1$, every $\beta\in(0,1]$ and every instance whose comparator satisfies $\LE(\beta)$, $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{65536\,b\,D(k,T,\bar\varepsilon)}\,R\,Q_\beta(k,T)$.

results.notes: Limit eps->0 gives ratio <= 65536 uniformly in T for fixed k.

source.label: cor:mixture
source.quote: It reads none of $m,\beta,T,\varepsilon$, and $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{b}\cdot\frac{R}{4608(\sqrt k+k/T)}$ (all $T\ge1$), $\E[\widehat{\ALG}_T]\ge\frac{a^2}{3072\,b}\cdot\frac{R\,q_\beta}{\PhiK(k)}$ ($T\ge16k$)

results.notes: Second line: 3072 b/a^2 Phi(K) K^gamma for T>=16K; noiseless: 3*2^19 Max(K^gamma,K/T). Not separately recorded.
